title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LORNA'S FIDDLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lorna Tolliver, a sock factory machine fixer in Mount Airy, North Carolina.
She can fix any machine with a wrench and a hard look.
But at fifty-nine, she had never played one note of music.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OLD CASE
segments.quote: You can't help getting older, but you don't have to get old.
segments.author: George Burns
lines: In her mom's attic, Lorna found Granddaddy Amos's old fiddle.
She was too old to learn now. Wasn't she?
Taped inside the case was a line from the comedian George Burns:
You can't help getting older, but you don't have to get old.
She bought new strings the next morning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SQUEAK
segments.quote: The easiest way to avoid wrong notes is to never open your mouth and sing. What a mistake that would be.
segments.author: Pete Seeger
lines: Her first note sounded like a cat in a screen door.
The neighbor's beagle howled along. Every night.
Lorna almost closed the case for good. Then she remembered the folk singer Pete Seeger:
The easiest way to avoid wrong notes is to never open your mouth and sing. What a mistake that would be.
So she kept squeaking.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: MISS ODELL
segments.quote: Wisdom is the reward you get for a lifetime of listening when you'd have preferred to talk.
segments.author: Doug Larson
lines: She went to Miss Odell, an eighty-eight-year-old fiddler who had played with Granddaddy.
Lorna talked for twenty minutes straight. Miss Odell said, Hush, and listen.
Odell had a line on her fridge from the columnist Doug Larson:
Wisdom is the reward you get for a lifetime of listening when you'd have preferred to talk.
So Lorna listened, and learned by ear.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SORE FINGERS
segments.quote: A genius? Perhaps, but before I was a genius I was a drudge.
segments.author: Ignacy Jan Paderewski
lines: Her fingertips got so sore, she typed her work reports with her knuckles.
On the break room wall hung a line from the Polish pianist Paderewski:
A genius? Perhaps, but before I was a genius I was a drudge.
So she played twenty minutes every day. Lunch break, rain or shine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BROKEN STRING
segments.quote: In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: At the Mount Airy fiddlers convention, halfway through her tune, a string snapped. Ping.
Two hundred people went quiet.
Then she heard Granddaddy's favorite line, from Albert Einstein:
In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.
She grinned, played on three strings, and stomped her boot. The crowd stomped with her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: FRIDAY NIGHTS
segments.quote: Music is the poetry of the air.
segments.author: Jean Paul
lines: She didn't win a ribbon. But a banjo man and two coworkers asked to play with her.
Now every Friday night, they jam on Lorna's porch, with Mom in Granddaddy's rocker.
Mom smiled and quoted the old German writer Jean Paul:
Music is the poetry of the air.
And the beagle still sings along.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Stay young. Play wrong notes. Listen. Practice. Use the trouble. Share the music.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Don't get old. Play the wrong notes. Listen more than you talk. Practice a little every day. Use the trouble. Share the music.
I tried the fiddle once. My cat left home.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
